messages:
Maria K.: deploy-bot just flagged a sustained error-rate bump in eu-west for canary v3.5.0, p95 latency also drifting. thoughts on auto vs manual fallback? :thinking:
Devon L.: saw the alert too. error rate ~2.7% over 10m, threshold was 2.0%. deploy-bot suggested fallback to stable-2026-02 for eu-west.
Ravi P.: can we do partial traffic split rather than full rollback? keep 20% new, 80% stable, watch for 15m?
Taylor S.: partial splits are fine but we need comms prepared for customers in eu. also need release-notes entry explaining the fallback and impact.
deploy-bot: AUTOMATED FALLBACK SUGGESTED -> action: route traffic eu-west -> stable-2026-02; reason: error_rate>threshold(2.0%), p95>latency_slo(250ms). to approve: react :white_check_mark:.
Maria K.: i'm leaning manual for now — want an ops hand to confirm logs and trace sample requests. Ravi, can you pull a few request traces? :eyes:
Ravi P.: on it. pulling traces from 14:32-14:45 UTC. two distinct error clusters: grpc 14:35-14:37 (auth token refresh) and model timeouts 14:40-14:44. looks like the new runtime has a KV cache race under load.
Taylor S.: if it's KV cache related we should fallback model variant (no-kv-cache) rather than full version revert. that reduces blast radius.
Maria K.: good point. Does deploy tooling support per-model-flag traffic pinning?
Devon L.: yes — we can route to "v3.5.0-no-kvcache" in eu-west only. command: `/deploy route --region=eu-west --target=v3.5.0-no-kvcache --percent=100` (ops-only).
SLO Monitor: Note: if we pin to no-kvcache variant, expected cost +3% and p95 may increase by ~20ms.
Maria K.: decision: do targeted variant pin (no-kvcache) in eu-west at t+10m, monitor 10m, rollback to stable only if errors persist. Ravi/Taylor please own verification and release-notes blurb. Sasha, can you draft a quick customer note in case we escalate?
Sasha (sales): will draft a short note: "Brief service degradation in EU; engineering applied targeted fallback to maintain service. No customer action required." share for signoff in #customer-alerts.
Ravi P.: traces show error cluster cleared after dropping KV caching on a sample canary. ready to execute when Maria gives a thumbs-up.
Maria K.: executing now. Devon/Taylor update observability widgets to surface the rollback signal and add alert for regression.
Devon L.: updated dashboards, added an ephemeral alert rule: eu-west variant-error-rate >1.5% for 5m -> paging oncall.
Taylor S.: release notes: "Applied targeted fallback in eu-west for v3.5.0 to mitigate transient KV cache errors; customers unaffected. Root cause investigation ongoing; follow-up postmortem planned." sending PR to release-notes repo.
deploy-bot: ACTION LOGGED: manual-route by Maria K. -> routed eu-west -> v3.5.0-no-kvcache at 14:56 UTC.
Maria K.: closing loop — will wait 30m then decide on permanent revert vs patch. creating ticket INF-4321 for postmortem and customer comms tracking. :white_check_mark:
Sasha (sales): will standby for any customer escalations and share draft in #customer-alerts for approval.
Ravi P.: leaving notes in INF-4321 with sample traces and suggested patch (KV lock guard).
Taylor S.: thanks all — clean handoff. will write short postmortem template tonight. :slightly_smiling_face:
